newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SALE OF TICKETS TO PATRIOTS' PLAYOFF GAME TURNS UGLY.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-SALE OF TICKETS TO PATRIOTS' PLAYOFF GAME TURNS UGLY.

text.p: The sale of tickets for Sunday's AFC Championship Game at Foxboro Stadium turned ugly Tuesday morning when some fans shut out of the NFL playoff game took to throwing rocks and bottles.
More than 7,000 fans showed up for the sale of 3,000 remaining seats for the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
The Patriots had announced that tickets for Sunday's game would go on sale at 10 a.m. and that fans would be allowed on the stadium complex at 6 a.m.

When the large crowd gathered, the team handed out vouchers for tickets that could be purchased in the afternoon. Fans unable to obtain vouchers argued with stadium officials and police, and incidents of rock and bottle throwing were reported.
Don Lowery, director of public relations for the Patriots, said the team was required to put tickets up for sale.
"In terms of distributing tickets this way, it certainly is not ideal. But we, the Patriots organisation, were doing what was required by law," Lowery said.
"The number one issue here was public safety and our plans changed because the crowds that assembled this morning posed a significant safety risk."
